verdict:
FLAT SURVIVES UNANIMOUSLY - but escalate, because every bench including blue mis-handled the series-basis problem, and the one disclosure that materially softens the damage read was caught by nobody.

WHAT I RE-FETCHED, PER BLUE-CORRECTIONS-AUDITED. The vetted 2Q26 exhibit, my own proxy-fetch. It prints: NPL 15-90 headline (gross portfolio incl. CC receivable anticipation): 4.3/4.1/4.0/4.3/4.1/4.1/4.0/4.6/4.8 (2Q24-2Q26) - so 2Q25=4.1, 2Q26=4.8, blue verbatim right, red's 3.9->4.3->4.5 is the expanded/ex-CC variant, and red's proposed re-anchor would have moved the 3Q tripwire onto the wrong basis. NPL>90 headline: 4.6 (2Q25) -> 5.3 (2Q26); expanded: 4.3 -> 5.0; and the YoY BRIDGE chart: 4.4% -> 5.1% (+53bps private payroll, +12bps other). Blue's 'thesis wrong on both ends' is therefore itself a series-selection overstatement - the thesis's 4.4->5.0/5.1 matches the vetted bridge and expanded bases. Nobody fabricated anything; the document speaks in three dialects and the pipeline has no series-pinning discipline.

THE FINDING NOBODY MADE, AND IT CHANGES THE DAMAGE MAGNITUDE. The same asset-quality page discloses: 'we adjusted the write-off of credit cards, resulting in a non-recurring impact of 30bps on the NPL ratio over 90 days, with no effect on the provision or cost of risk levels.' Thirty basis points of the NPL>90 level is a WRITE-OFF-POLICY artifact, not credit formation. Stack the bridge: of the ~65-70bps YoY deterioration, 53bps is the private-payroll seasoning (named, bounded, insured as of August), ~12bps is everything else, and ~30bps of the LEVEL is policy. The ex-payroll, ex-artifact residual deterioration in the core book is approximately zero to slightly negative - the core is not deteriorating. That does not make INTR cheap (1.16x book at 16.3% ROE against a ~15.5-17% BRL cost of equity is fair, full stop) and it does not flip DAMAGE-ARRIVING (payroll seasoning is real, CoR 5.0->5.9 is real, coverage 143->134 is real if partly mechanical mix-dilution). But it means the November tripwires were about to be armed against numbers containing a disclosed one-time distortion, and it softens the bear's formation story at the margin.

WHERE THE NAME LANDS. Fair-not-cheap, idiosyncratically de-rated ~27-30pp vs actual Brazilian peers (blue's corrected peer tape: ITUB -23%, NU -20% off highs - red's -10%/stable figures failed tape-verify), with one named, bounded, actively-mitigated problem product and an election-macro overlay into October. The re-anchored 3Q refutation test survives with my re-pinning below. The existing ledger gate (alert_below 4.5, REVIEW-ONLY at ~1.0x book) is correctly conditioned - it triggers a decomposition, not an entry - and passes the beta-carrier test only because it is explicitly informational; a bare entry gate at 4.5 would NOT pass (the carrier is Brazil risk premium + BRL into an election).

WHY ESCALATE RATHER THAN CLOSE: (1) blue's correction of red was right on 15-90 but overconfident on 90+, and only an adjudicator re-fetch caught it - the CLSK lesson (audit blue) fired again, one batch later, in the subtler form of series-selection rather than outright error. (2) The 30bps disclosure was missed by triage, red, AND blue in a document all three fetched - a three-bench read-through failure on the page their dispute was about. (3) The 3Q tripwire set must be re-pinned before the pack arms, and that is an action item on a live WATCH row.
blue_ruling: PARTIALLY OVERTURNED - and then the adjudicator's re-fetch partially overturned the overturn. Blue correctly showed red's strongest kill (the 4.5% NPL re-anchor) was itself a wrong-basis artifact: red's series is the expanded/ex-credit-card sub-series and the thesis's 4.8% endpoint IS the vetted headline. My proxy-fetch of the vetted exhibit confirms both series digit-for-digit. But blue's own NPL>90 correction ('thesis wrong on both ends, 4.6 to 5.3') overstates: the same exhibit prints an NPL>90 YoY BRIDGE of 4.4% to 5.1% - the thesis's exact numbers, on the bridge basis. Three NPL>90 presentations coexist in one document and each bench picked a different one while accusing the others of error. And BOTH benches missed a disclosed 30bps non-recurring write-off-policy impact sitting in the same paragraph.
reopen_gates: DATA (the re-pinned 3Q26 refutation test - series labels are part of the gate): on the HEADLINE gross-portfolio basis: NPL 15-90 <= 4.8% AND cost of risk <= 6.0% AND coverage >= 134% AND ROE >= 16%, with NPL>90 read EX the disclosed 30bps write-off artifact (i.e., compare like-for-like or use the company's own bridge) -> flip toward damage-absent, re-court for a starter. Bear confirmation: headline 15-90 > 5.0% with coverage < 130%.

DATA (interim, free, monthly): BCB Credito do Trabalhador / monthly credit statistics reading the private-payroll vintage curve directly - flattening delinquency there front-runs the 3Q print by weeks.

EVENT: the August-2026 private-payroll credit insurance + DataPrev auto-relinkage showing up as a disclosed CoR or NPL-formation improvement - the fix is currently untested; first evidence it works is a genuine thesis change.

PRICE (existing ledger gate, KEPT AS-IS because it is correctly conditioned): alert_below 4.5 (~1.0x 2Q26 book) as a REVIEW-ONLY decomposition trigger, never entry - price weakness into the October election is presumptively thesis-worse (macro carrier), so any fill must be decomposed before action.

DATA (before any sizing ever): product-level coverage decomposition from the 20-F/BCB SCR - the coverage 143->134 'unbooked-provision tell' remains PLAUSIBLE-only until the mechanical mix-dilution share is separated; both benches endorsed this gap, neither closed it.
process_flags: ESCALATE (reason 1 - BLUE'S CORRECTION NEEDED ITS OWN AUDIT, second consecutive batch): blue rightly overturned red's wrong-basis re-anchor on NPL 15-90 (adjudicator-verified: 4.8 IS the vetted headline), but blue's parallel claim that the thesis's NPL>90 numbers were 'wrong on both ends' is a series-selection overstatement - the vetted exhibit's own YoY bridge prints 4.4%->5.1%, the thesis's numbers. The CLSK/SPRY doctrine held: no bench's correction entered this verdict unfetched.

ESCALATE (reason 2 - THREE-BENCH READ-THROUGH MISS ON THE DISPUTED PAGE): the 30bps non-recurring credit-card write-off-policy impact on NPL>90 is disclosed in the same asset-quality section every bench quoted, and none surfaced it. It re-scales the core-book deterioration to approximately zero ex-payroll ex-artifact. The tripwires were about to be armed against distorted numbers on a live WATCH row - action item, not observation.

ESCALATE (reason 3 - TAPE-VERIFY FAILURE INSIDE A BENCH): red's peer-tape figures (ITUB ~-10%, NU stable) failed blue's tape-verify (actual: -23% and -20% off highs). Direction survived, magnitude did not. FCT.MI discipline fired on a bench, not just a thesis - log it in the bench-quality record.
